dedupe_keys.name: great east japan earthquake cost and efficiency of disaster waste disposal by municipality

description: This case study analyses what drove the cost and efficiency of disposing of the waste left by the Great East Japan Earthquake and tsunami of March 2011. Toshiaki Sasao of Iwate University published it in Waste Management in 2017. Two analyses were run on municipal disposal data: an ordinary least squares regression of the factors that affect disposal costs, and a two-stage data envelopment analysis of each municipality's efficiency to identify best performance in disaster waste management. The article is available online by subscription, and the abstract is free on PubMed. Coverage is the municipalities that managed disaster waste after the event. Caveats: the author notes that radioactive contamination from the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear power station likely influenced the results, and municipal cost data are not published with the article. A higher recycling rate of disaster waste and a larger amount of tsunami sediment lowered average disposal cost, while area-wide management raised it; efficiency varied widely between municipalities, and more temporary incinerators and secondary waste stocks improved efficiency scores. Simulation uses: cost drivers and efficiency benchmarks for post-disaster debris and waste management models. Related records: the Minami-Ise pre-disaster waste planning study (case_study-minami-ise-pre-disaster-waste-management-lca-lcc) plans for a future event, and the CRS report on disaster debris management (data-crs-disaster-debris-management-r44941) covers US practice.
